hooks.A: The story of Instagram: thirteen employees, one billion dollars, eighteen months.
hooks.B: The story of Instagram. Spoiler: it started as an app nobody wanted.
hooks.C: The story of Instagram: how thirteen people sold an app for one billion dollars.

lines.text: But this app started as a total flop.
In 2010, Kevin Systrom built an app called Burbn.
He even raised five hundred thousand dollars from investors to build it.
You could check in to places, make plans, and share photos.
The problem? It was confusing, and it didn't take off.
Then he teamed up with Mike Krieger, and they noticed something.
People ignored the check-ins. But they loved sharing photos.
So they cut everything else. Just photos, filters, and likes.
They renamed it Instagram, and launched on the iPhone in October 2010.
It exploded. By 2012, around thirty million people were using it.
In April 2012, Facebook agreed to buy Instagram for about one billion dollars.
For a company with just thirteen employees.
And it all started with a failed app called Burbn.
